question: Under the capacity limit, does weighting each scored position's KL by the candidate student's own Top-200 uncertainty select a structural initialization that, after the frozen recovery recipe, recovers more autonomous task correctness than the standing incumbent B?

motivation.title: capacity-aware student reasoning
motivation.premise: The teacher (Qwen3-4B-Thinking) and the ~0.6B student differ in capacity, expressiveness and learning ability. The student need not, and may not be able to, reproduce the teacher's reasoning distribution; on some tasks it may reach the same correct answer by a shorter, simpler or entirely different trajectory.
motivation.consequence: A large teacher token-level KL does not by itself mean worse student reasoning. KL-based compression selection may over-reward structures that imitate the teacher's distribution and under-rate structures that preserve the student's own effective way of reasoning.
motivation.question: Which structural initialization, under the capacity limit, best lets the student keep and recover its own effective reasoning ability?
motivation.role_of_confidence: the student's Top-K confidence is a CANDIDATE PROXY signal for structure selection. Its value is decided by independent behavioural evidence, never assumed

hypothesis: The more certain the student is of its own prediction at a position, the weaker the KL penalty for differing from the teacher there should be. This does NOT assume the student is right where it is confident; it tests whether relaxing strict imitation of the teacher's distribution helps a small model keep computation and reasoning suited to its own capacity.

objective.formula: L(x) = (1/T_x) sum_{t in T_x} (1 - c_t) KL_t, minimized

acts_directly_on: global state evaluation of every child
does_not_act_on: FFN, residual WIDTH and ATTENTION operator-local selection: they keep D1's target-aware activation statistic unchanged; their children are reached by the objective only through state evaluation and the beam
scope.do_not_claim: that the local rules of all four operators use student confidence
scope.intermediate_vs_final_student: the confidence the search reads belongs to INTERMEDIATE candidates -- the parent with some layers bypassed in DEPTH, partially compressed children in state evaluation -- before any recovery training. It is not the confidence of the final ~0.6B student after recovery, and it is not evidence about that model's capacity adaptation; only the behavioural evaluation after recovery speaks to that

aggregation_control.issue: revision 2 averaged state-evaluation items EQUALLY, where D1's KL-only state metrics weight items by scored positions within a sub-type and pool critical classes over items. That changed length weighting as well as the integrand, so a D1-vs-D2 ranking change could not be attributed to confidence
aggregation_control.resolution: each consumer keeps its KL-only path's weighting (objective identity field `aggregation`, kl_path_weighting_per_consumer/v2): DEPTH averages items equally, as D1's DEPTH did; state evaluation weights items by T_x and pools critical classes. The per-item formula keeps the fixed 1/T_x and never divides by a sum of confidence weights
aggregation_control.built_in_kl_only_control: every objective evaluation also reports state.objective.raw_kl.* -- the raw KL aggregated exactly as the objective is -- which equals D1's state.teacher_kl.* and state.critical_token_kl in the same evaluation (tested to 1e-6). Rankings by raw_kl and by the objective on the same states isolate the effect of the integrand

one_variable.changed_from_d1: the scoring objective of DEPTH, state evaluation and the beam ranking -- and only that
unchanged: frozen operator set and calibration-profile assignment space

beam._why_unchanged: the standing declared schedule. D1/D2/D3 share a beam width so the BREADTH is not a variable between them, and adopting a different one here would be a new breadth decision taken for no measured reason.

search.measurer: StateEvaluator with the SAME scoring objective; BeamSearch refuses any mismatch

execution.prediction_rows: all_v1, unless R0's verdict is PASS and recorded before the search authorization, then scored_v1. An execution choice validated equivalent, recorded in the run's execution fingerprint; it changes no estimand

retention.rule: Diversity is used only during search-time beam pruning. Final post-search Top-K must NOT use lineage diversity.
retention.post_search: epsilon-Pareto quality order + deterministic tie-break -> NO lineage diversity
retention.order: OBJECTIVE_PARETO_V1 quality order over complete leaves, deterministic tie-break; no lineage diversity

search_diagnostics.kl_only_control: every state carries state.objective.raw_kl.* (equal to D1's state.teacher_kl.*) beside the objective; the D1 ranking of D2's complete leaves under PARETO_V1 on those raw-KL metrics is reported, never used
search_diagnostics.per_candidate: DEPTH records objective, raw KL, entropy, confidence, uncertainty weight, Top-K mass, reference tail mass and joint histograms for every candidate subset
search_diagnostics.flags: diagnostic_threshold_rule, thresholds from the reference calibration frozen BEFORE this search; computed offline; never a selection rule
search_diagnostics.no_third_kl_only_search: the KL-only comparison is the built-in control on D2's own states and D1's completed search -- not a new search

screening.comparator: B's two imported screening units -- not retrained, not regenerated

rule.statistic: pooled seed-mean correct_overall delta vs B, C0's guardrail vetoes
rule.selection: exactly one candidate advances, or none
rule.tie_break: the experiment's frozen quality position, then state id
rule.field: frozen by the experiment's own retention decision before any behavioural datum; its size is that experiment's preregistered choice
rule.q2_screening_rows: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. q2 advanced on these prompts and seeds, so its screening estimate is inflated by the winner's curse (screening +0.00825 vs B, confirmation -0.000392). Never a ranking comparator

confirmation.candidate: exactly the one screening advances, or none
confirmation.secondary: q2's three imported units, descriptive only

outcomes.SHARED_GO: one-sided (1 - per_experiment_alpha) LCB > 0 AND delta >= SESOI AND >= 2 of 3 seed deltas > 0 AND no guardrail veto. NOT a promotion: it nominates the candidate for a fresh independent confirmation on its reserved battery
outcomes.NO_GO: one-sided (1 - per_experiment_alpha) UCB < SESOI, or a guardrail veto. Terminal for that candidate
outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: otherwise. Terminal; never rerun on these rows

instruments.rollout_profile: scripts/stages/stage-1/families/d_series/rollout_profile.py -- text-level, $0, from secured generations: generated length (engine count), reasoning/answer length, natural termination, degeneration, correctness by reasoning length, and paired same-prompt comparisons
instruments.rollout_rescoring: scripts/shared/evaluation/rollout_rescoring.py -- per position of the student's own rollout: student confidence, student token log-prob, teacher surprisal, KL(teacher || student). Needs the trained checkpoint, so it runs ON THE POD after generation and before the checkpoint is released. Reads generations; changes neither generation nor scoring, so the shared evaluation protocol's identity is untouched. Estimated 3-5 GPU-minutes per probe (~0.95M tokens per probe at D1's measured lengths)

analyses.question: does the student still solve the task when it is far from the teacher's distribution?
analyses.instrument: rollout_rescoring (per sample: mean KL and teacher surprisal on its own rollout) joined to correctness

analyses.question: autonomous reasoning length, correctness and usable rollout
analyses.arms: every unit, including the imported B/q2 (baseline recorded in analyses/d1_rollout_profile.json)

analyses.question: how does student confidence relate to actual correctness?
analyses.instrument: rollout_rescoring confidence (reasoning and answer spans) against per-sample correctness

analyses.question: are high-confidence, high-KL positions valid alternative reasoning or wrong overconfidence?
analyses.instrument: rollout_rescoring quadrant fraction against correctness; thresholds registered in each experiment's preregistration before any result, none in code

analyses.question: did D2/D3 improve autonomous generation after recovery, not only the search objective?
analyses.instrument: the shared-protocol endpoint and the rollout profile against B (and q2), read beside each candidate's search objective and raw KL
analyses.arms: candidates vs the imported B/q2 units

diagnostics.historical_units: B's and q2's ten units have decoded text and the engine's token counts, but NO token ids, log-probabilities or logits, and their checkpoints are retired. Their student confidence on their own rollouts is therefore NOT available and must not be estimated or inferred; comparisons with B/q2 are text-level and endpoint-level only. Re-tokenizing their text reproduces the engine's count exactly for 82-85% of samples
diagnostics.power_note: D1's units answer ~2-4% of scorable prompts correctly (B: 103 of 2550 on confirmation), and q2 and B are both right on only 29 prompt-seeds there. Any confidence-correctness or quadrant analysis rests on ~100 correct samples per arm and is exploratory

rescoring_integration.token_ids: use the generation engine's exact ids, kept by the read-only sidecar wrapper scripts/shared/evaluation/uncapped_eval_token_ids.py. It runs the UNCHANGED in-tree generator (same argv, interpreter and environment) with a hook on the one post-wave decode per record, after the engine loop, so the generation source set, the generation fingerprint and the shared protocol's evaluation identity are the plain run's -- tested on the real generator with a stub engine: identical records, summaries and reconstructed fingerprint. The hook installs only when the generator's source digest equals the protocol's; every row is verified against its record (id count, prompt count, decoded-text sha256, EOS vs stop_reason) and the sidecar header says whether the stratum is exact. A record with no exact row is rescored from retokenized text, ids_source=retokenized_text, labelled approximate per sample. Recording ids inside the generator itself remains a VERSIONED decision (d_series_shared_eval v2), not taken

token_ids_identity.changes: only the behavioural driver's own executable closure, because its argv names the wrapper -- correct for reproducibility, and not part of the generation identity
token_ids_identity.not_in_generation_source_set: the wrapper is deliberately NOT added to source_sets.json generation.files: adding it would move the source digest it exists to preserve
token_ids_identity.residual: engine scheduling is timing-dependent in the plain run too; the wrapper adds no work inside the engine loop, so it changes no code path the tokens depend on, but token equality with a counterfactual plain run cannot be proven on a non-batch-invariant engine

alignment_evidence: count and decoded-text match with the record
untouched: the shared protocol's scoring contract and endpoint
rescoring_integration.checkpoint_release: only after the diagnostic evidence is persisted durably, when a consumer exists
rescoring_integration.failure_isolation: a rescoring failure is recorded per sample and never alters or blocks a completed per-sample score (rollout_rescoring.rescore_unit)
rescoring_integration.cost: MEASURE before pricing: the reference calibration session times the rescoring on the real teacher and B over sequences of D1's measured lengths; the behavioural ceiling includes it only after that measurement. The 3-5 min/probe figure is an estimate, not a bound
rescoring_integration.historical_units: no logits, confidence or student-side quantity is computed or estimated for B or q2

prerequisites.why: diagnostic thresholds must be frozen before any D2 candidate exists; D3's lambda is measured in the same pass
freezes K and every rule above

prerequisites.what: a search price under the per-session ceiling
prerequisites.why: priced from D1's own search records, the planning bound exceeds the per-session ceiling while DEPTH is priced at D1's recompute-mode maxima; it fits once the reference cache's allocator-hoard fix is shown on a GPU (the reference calibration's stage L), or by a maintainer cap decision
D2 must not strand D3 or a fresh confirmation

claim_boundary.goal: structural initializations that, under the capacity limit, help the student keep and recover its own effective reasoning
may_claim: a D2/D3 candidate's endpoint result against B on the shared protocol, with that protocol's limits (SHARED_GO nominates, never promotes)
descriptive rollout and rescoring diagnostics of the candidates that were actually measured, labelled exploratory
may_not_claim: that a lower D2/D3 search objective means better reasoning or higher fidelity
that the student reasons differently, or better, where it is confident and far from the teacher, without rollout-level evidence linking those positions to correct completions
any confidence or per-position statement about B or q2, whose checkpoints are retired and whose generations carry no log-probabilities
a mechanism from the exploratory diagnostics alone
that the local selection rules of all four operators use student confidence (only DEPTH's does; see objective_scope)
that confidence read on intermediate search candidates describes the final recovered student's capacity adaptation

that the family-wise bound across D1-D3 is an unconditional guarantee: it is a nominal accounting bound, conditional on each test's nominal level, which adaptive reuse of the observed confirmation data can violate
claim_boundary.validation: Top-K confidence is a proxy for structure selection; its usefulness is established only by independent behavioural evidence after recovery training

measured_basis.source: logs/stages/stage-1/phase_d1/runs/d1_search_20261006_210210/closeout/outcome.json: 92/92 expansions, same space, support, beam and L40S

objective_overhead.source: provisional -- an estimate, not a measurement

calibration_evidence.why: no stage-L session is booked with evidence

cache_fix.what: `_available_memory_bytes` returns the allocator's hoard (empty_cache) before reading the driver: D1's search recomputed the reference in 15/16 DEPTH expansions with 0.12 GiB free and 36 GiB reclaimable
cache_fix._validated_on_gpu_is: DERIVED from the booked, hash-verified stage-L evidence above; never set by hand
cache_fix.validated_by: stage L's DEPTH pair, which runs under a deliberately hoarded pool and records reference_cache.mode; or D2's own first DEPTH expansions
cache_fix.until_validated: the planning bound prices DEPTH at D1's measured recompute-mode maxima

previous_model_superseded.why: D1's design priced DEPTH from a8's one CACHED invocation (1194 s); D1's own search then recomputed the reference cache in 15 of 16 DEPTH expansions, up to 2486 s. The records model takes DEPTH from that search, and applies the objective's overhead to the two paths it touches instead of x1.10 on every structural minute

assumptions_not_measured: the objective's added seconds per DEPTH candidate and per state evaluation: +5% of D1's mean (expected) and +10% (planning bound) until stage L measures them
D2's trajectory has D1's size (92 expansions, 16 DEPTH): the beam schedule fixes the expansion count, not the operator mix
d2_search.hard_is: a PLANNING BOUND from D1's measured maxima, not a proven bound on runtime. What bounds MONEY is the enforceable stop below; the bound decides only whether the search is expected to FINISH inside it

enforceable_stop.set_at: the D2 search authorization, at the live rate
enforceable_stop.mechanism: the launcher's session cap: the watchdog kills the pod at the plan's hard-terminate minutes and the driver's soft stop fails the search closed before it, so spend stops at the cap whatever the runtime

d2_search._basis: expected = D1's measured 551.99 min + the objective's expected added minutes over D1's trajectory; bound = D1's search_cost on the records-rebuilt cost model

budget.enforceable_stop: each session's authorization caps spend at the live rate; planning bounds are not the cap
